headline: Indian Hockey Captain Declares He Only Scores Braces Because Prime Numbers Give Him Anxiety
body:
The Indian men's hockey team captain confirmed today that his consistent habit of scoring exactly two goals per match is a strategic move to avoid the mental instability he associates with prime numbers. Speaking after his latest brace, the captain noted that finishing with a total of three or five goals would disrupt his equilibrium for the rest of the tournament.

“Anything other than an even pair feels mathematically cluttered,” explained the team’s lead sports psychologist, Dr. Ramesh Varma, who has been training the squad to view the hockey pitch as a giant, symmetrical graph. “When he scores once, he feels a crushing need to balance the scoreboard, like a man who has accidentally put on two different colored socks.”

Opposition teams have reportedly expressed confusion, with Welsh defenders claiming they were prepared for high-octane attacks but weren't ready for a striker who apologizes every time he accidentally misses a second shot. The team management is now debating whether to allow a third goal if the match situation becomes dire, though they worry it might trigger a full-scale existential crisis for the captain.
